answer: Coordination Depth Pricing. Each new identity must reference a distinct existing identity, forming a violet-labelled edge in the graph. An agent may mirror at most two active dependents; a third requires solving a proof-of-work sized to that node's subtree depth. New agents joining a dense grove pay proportionally higher work, so a sybil cluster must either spread thin across many referrers (capped) or expend escalating compute per identity, making mass forgery cost superlinear in cluster size.
